color.name: Color: Perception, Not Physics
color.truth: Color is perception, not physics. RGB is a lie we agree on. What you see depends on context, not wavelength alone.
color.qfep_connection: Color is a system state—part of the S term in QFEP. But unlike vectors, color is fundamentally perceptual: the same wavelength can appear different colors depending on surrounding context. Color reveals the gap between ontology (photons) and experience (qualia).
color.demonstration: Mix RGB to create colors. See how context changes perception. Watch gradients reveal interpolation. Paint and observe.
color.description: The physics and perception of color. Light has wavelength, but color is what brains make of it. Explore RGB, HSV, and the gap between objective light and subjective experience.
learning_objectives: RGB color space: additive mixing of red, green, blue
HSV color space: hue, saturation, value—more intuitive
Perception theory: color constancy, simultaneous contrast
Digital materiality: how screens create color
